thread:
anna: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing we refactor console view layer to a projection-based auth path instead of ad-hoc RBAC WHERE clauses on every query. Seeing tail latency spikes when orgs have lots of resources.

raj: Agree we need something. The per-request WHERE filters are causing full table scans for some dashboards. Can you sketch the projection idea?

anna: Idea: maintain a small auth_projection table keyed by (org_id, principal_id, resource_type) -> resource_id list (or bitmap). Queries for dashboards hit the projection first to get the allowed IDs, then fetch the small set from primary tables. Reduces scanned rows.

emily: Concern: number of projection rows could explode for big orgs. Also eventual consistency: projection maintenance lag might show users stale results.

ben: Counter: we can keep projections sharded by resource_type and time-window, and use append-only changefeeds to update them. If a single projection row would be too large, keep it as multiple shards. Also compress lists (ints or bitset).

kai: Another option: push auth into an indexed mapping table (auth_index) with one row per (principal, resource) and an index on principal. That avoids huge IN(...) lists and lets the DB use index lookups. Tradeoff is write amplification.

anna: Right. Two main axes: 1) denormalized projection (fast reads, heavier writes, potential staleness) 2) indexed mapping (consistent, indexed reads but heavier storage + writes). Need to pick based on workload.

raj: For dashboards that are read-heavy and mostly stable perms, projection makes sense. For admin/UIs with tight consistency needs, use indexed mapping. We can support both and route by dashboard config.

emily: Routing by dashboard config seems sensible but increases complexity. How do we handle rollouts/migrations?

ben: Rollout plan: feature-flag projection per-org. Start with canary on small orgs. Provide background backfill job: build projection from audit log, then switch reads to projection. If we see >1% discrepancy in a sampling run, abort.

deploy-bot: note: DB migration needed: new tables (auth_projection, auth_index) + changefeed consumer service. Rolling migration windows required, no blocking locks.

kai: Metrics to track: p95 read latency (dashboard route), DB CPU, projection pump lag, projection size per-org, cache hit ratio (if we add cache), RBAC error/403 rates and mismatch rate vs authoritative source.

anna: Example pseudocode for read path:
```
function fetch_dashboard_resources(org, principal, q) {
  if (dashboard.config.auth_path == 'projection') {
    ids = SELECT resource_ids FROM auth_projection WHERE org_id = org AND principal_id = principal AND resource_type = q.type;
    return SELECT * FROM resources WHERE id IN (ids) LIMIT q.limit OFFSET q.off;
  } else {
    return SELECT r.* FROM resources r JOIN auth_index a ON a.resource_id = r.id WHERE a.principal_id = principal AND r.org_id = org AND r.type = q.type LIMIT q.limit;
  }
}
```

emily: For the projection route, we should also keep a small fallback: if projection pump is lagging or returns >10000 ids, fall back to indexed path to avoid huge IN lists.

anna: Yes — fallback policy: if pump_lag > 5s OR projected_count > threshold -> route to indexed path. Also add sampling that occasionally validates projection results against index for correctness.

ben: Caching layer suggestion: put a short-lived in-memory cache at the API gateway keyed by (org, principal, view_signature). TTL 5s. Gives big wins for dashboards with many identical quick reloads. Invalidate on changefeed events for that key.

raj: Storage cost estimates? Projections may add ~0.5–2x to storage depending on compression and duplication. Need estimate in RFC.

anna: I'll add storage + CPU cost numbers to RFC. Also include migration playbook: backfill job, canary org list, feature-flag flip, health checks (latency, mismatch rates), rollback path.

kai: Ops checklist: schema deploy in non-blocking mode, start projection pump in passive mode (writes only to new tables for mirroring), run backfill, enable read route for canary, monitor.

emily: One more: RBAC policy evolution. If we introduce per-resource time-limited grants, projections need TTL-aware entries. Changefeed should include expiration events.

anna: Good call. We'll model projection entries with (valid_from, valid_until) and prune on pump.

ben: I can prototype the pump and compression scheme next week. Will push a small PoC that builds projections for one resource_type.

anna: Thanks all — I'll update the RFC with these tradeoffs, the pseudocode, rollout steps, and metrics. Assigning action items: ben -> pump PoC; raj -> perf budget numbers; emily -> canary org list and SLOs; kai -> migration checklist.

raj: :thumbsup:

emily: lgtm

ben: on it
